Validates the type of an underscore-named anonymous field, allowing only anonymous struct/union types or paths, and emits an error for other types. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.
Rejects anonymous struct or union types in disallowed contexts by identifying which kind it is and emitting an error. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.
Rejects underscore-named anonymous fields in contexts where they are not allowed by emitting an error. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.

Rejects `const` functions declared in trait or trait-impl contexts where they are not permitted, computes suggestions to remove `const` or make the enclosing trait/impl const, and emits the diagnostic. It explicitly calls `constness` and `dcx` from the Methods List.

Runs the main function-signature validation checks in sequence. It explicitly calls `check_decl_num_args`, `check_decl_cvaradic_pos`, `check_decl_attrs`, and `check_decl_self_param` from the Methods List.
Ensures a function declaration does not exceed the maximum supported number of parameters and emits a fatal error if it does. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.
Checks that C-variadic `...` parameters are not the only parameter and appear only in the final position, emitting errors otherwise. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.

Validates attributes on function parameters, permitting only selected built-in lint/config attrs and rejecting doc comments or other forbidden built-in attrs with diagnostics. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.
Rejects a leading `self` parameter when the surrounding function context does not allow self semantics. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.
Rejects `default` in contexts where it is forbidden by computing an appropriate head span and emitting an error. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.
Returns the span of a trailing semicolon if one is present at the end of the given span; otherwise returns the span's high endpoint. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Rejects type bounds in a context that does not permit them by computing the combined bounds span and emitting an error. It explicitly calls `dcx` from the Methods List.

Validates that an extern type has neither generic parameters nor `where` clauses, reporting each forbidden component relative to the current extern block. It explicitly calls `dcx` and `current_extern_span` from the Methods List.
Rejects non-function foreign items that incorrectly include a body, emitting an error tied to the current extern block. It explicitly calls `dcx` and `current_extern_span` from the Methods List.
Rejects foreign functions that incorrectly include a body, emitting an error tied to the current extern block. It explicitly calls `dcx` and `current_extern_span` from the Methods List.
Returns the head span of the currently active extern block, assuming `extern_mod` is set. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Checks that an extern function declaration has no qualifiers in its header. If qualifiers are present, it emits an error using `current_extern_span` to reference the enclosing extern block.
Validates that a foreign item name is ASCII-only. On failure, it emits an error tied to `current_extern_span`.

Validates use of C-variadic parameters in a function-like item: rejects `const` with C variadics and requires the allowed foreign or `unsafe extern "C"` forms. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Rejects items named `_` for item kinds that must have a real name. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Ensures an item marked `#[no_mangle]` has an ASCII identifier, computing a head span for diagnostics when needed. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Ensures a module item intended for file loading has an ASCII identifier. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Rejects generic parameters in contexts where they are forbidden, such as auto traits. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Emits the shared E0568-style diagnostic for auto-trait bounds-related invalid syntax. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Rejects supertrait bounds in a forbidden context by computing the offending span and calling `emit_e0568`.
Rejects a non-empty where-clause in a forbidden context by calling `emit_e0568`.
Rejects associated items in a context where no items are allowed, collecting spans for a grouped diagnostic. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Builds a reordered generic-argument suggestion string with lifetimes first, regular arguments next, and associated constraints last. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Validates that generic arguments appear before associated constraints in angle-bracketed arguments. When invalid, it emits a diagnostic and calls `correct_generic_order_suggestion` to construct a fix suggestion.

Performs shared validation for type nodes: checks bare function types, duplicate trait-object lifetime bounds, banned or nested `impl Trait`, and requires at least one trait bound on `impl Trait`. It calls `check_fn_decl` and `maybe_lint_missing_abi`.
Buffers the `MISSING_ABI` lint for extern-like syntax that omitted an explicit ABI, while avoiding some macro-generated false positives. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Checks ordering of generic parameters so lifetimes come before type/const parameters, and prepares a reordered suggestion plus diagnostics for out-of-order cases. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Validates a single attribute node via the parser-side attribute checker. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Validates a type node, then continues traversal. It calls `visit_ty_common`, `deny_anon_struct_or_union`, and `walk_ty`.
Validates a label identifier and then walks the label subtree. It calls `check_label`.
Validates a lifetime identifier and then walks the lifetime subtree. It calls `check_lifetime`.
Validates a struct or union field definition, rejecting unnamed-field forms where disallowed, then walks the field. It calls `deny_unnamed_field`.

Validates top-level items with context-sensitive rules for impls, traits, functions, foreign modules, visibility, `#[no_mangle]`, `~const`, and ABI-related checks, while managing validator state during traversal. It calls `check_nomangle_item_asciionly`, `with_in_trait_impl`, `visibility_not_permitted`, `with_tilde_const`, `visit_generics`, `visit_trait_ref`, `visit_ty`, `check_defaultness`, `visit_fn`, and `maybe_lint_missing_abi`.

Validates items inside an extern block, enforcing bodylessness, generic restrictions, header restrictions, and ASCII-only names as appropriate for each foreign item kind. It calls `check_defaultness`, `check_foreign_fn_bodyless`, `check_foreign_fn_headerless`, `check_foreign_item_ascii_only`, `check_foreign_kind_bodyless`, `check_type_no_bounds`, and `check_foreign_ty_genericless`.

Validates generic-argument lists, enforcing argument/constraint ordering and allowing nested `impl Trait` only in associated-type-binding-like positions. It calls `check_generic_args_before_constraints`, `visit_generic_arg`, `with_impl_trait`, `visit_assoc_constraint`, and `visit_ty`.

Validates generic parameter defaults, parameter ordering, equality constraints, and nested higher-ranked lifetime syntax in where-clauses, then traverses parameters and predicates. It calls `validate_generic_param_order`, `deny_equality_constraints`, and `visit_where_predicate`.
Validates a generic parameter, specifically checking lifetime parameter names before walking the parameter. It calls `check_lifetime`.

Validates a single generic bound, enforcing restrictions on optional traits, const trait-object bounds, `~const` usage contexts, polarity, and malformed associated-constraint placement before continuing traversal. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Validates function declarations and function-context rules: `self` parameter legality, C-variadic restrictions, invalid `const async`/`const gen`, missing ABI linting, bodiless-pattern restrictions, and `~const` scoping before traversal. It calls `check_fn_decl`, `check_c_variadic_type`, `maybe_lint_missing_abi`, and `with_tilde_const`.

Validates associated items in traits and impls, including `#[no_mangle]` ASCII checks, defaultness, required bodies in impl items, type-bound restrictions, deprecated where-clause placement, visibility restrictions, trait-const restrictions, item naming, and context-sensitive `~const` state before traversal. It calls `check_nomangle_item_asciionly`, `check_defaultness`, `check_type_no_bounds`, `check_type_alias_where_clause_location`, `visibility_not_permitted`, `check_trait_fn_not_const`, `check_item_named`, `visit_vis`, `visit_ident`, `visit_fn`, `with_tilde_const`, and `with_in_trait_impl`.

Rejects equality constraints in where-clauses and attempts to synthesize trait-bound style suggestions, especially for associated-type equality forms. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Constructs an `AstValidator` with the initial validation state, walks the entire crate to perform AST validation, and returns whether proc-macro declarations were seen. It explicitly calls `walk_crate` to traverse the crate.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ast_lowering/src/lib.rs::: Formats an `ImplTraitPosition` as a user-facing descriptive string by matching the enum variant and writing the chosen text with `write!`.

Builds an index from local def-ids to their owning AST nodes for the crate and nested items. It creates the `Indexer` with `IndexVec::new`, seeds the crate entry via `ensure_contains_elem`, then traverses the AST by calling `visit::walk_crate`, which dispatches into the visitor methods `visit_item`, `visit_assoc_item`, and `visit_foreign_item` while skipping attribute lowering through `visit_attribute`.
Intentionally ignores attributes so expressions inside attributes are not indexed or lowered; it does not call other methods in this file.
Registers an AST item as the owner for its def-id in the index by calling `ensure_contains_elem`, then continues recursive traversal by calling `visit::walk_item`.
Registers an associated item as the owner for its def-id in the index by calling `ensure_contains_elem`, then continues recursive traversal by calling `visit::walk_assoc_item`.
Registers a foreign item as the owner for its def-id in the index by calling `ensure_contains_elem`, then continues recursive traversal by calling `visit::walk_item`.

Computes a stable crate HIR fingerprint by collecting owner entries, pairing each with its `def_path_hash` via `tcx.hir().def_path_hash`, sorting them with `sort_unstable_by_key`, and hashing the result inside `tcx.with_stable_hashing_context` using `StableHasher::new`, `hash_stable`, and `finish`.

Drives AST-to-HIR lowering for the whole crate. It first forces prerequisite queries with `ensure_with_value`, obtains and steals the resolver/AST pair, calls `index_crate` to build the AST owner index, allocates the owner table with `IndexVec::from_fn_n`, lowers each indexed owner by calling `item::ItemLowerer::lower_node`, drops AST data to free memory, and conditionally calls `compute_hir_hash` when `tcx.needs_crate_hash()` is true.

Creates and records a new local definition for an AST node. It first checks for an existing mapping by calling `opt_local_def_id`, uses `local_def_id` and `self.tcx.hir().def_key(...)` in the assertion message if one exists, then creates the def with `self.tcx.at(span).create_def(...).def_id()` and records it with `resolver.node_id_to_def_id.insert(...)`.
Allocates the next fresh AST `NodeId` from the resolver counter by calling `as_u32`, `checked_add`, `expect`, and `ast::NodeId::from_u32`, then updates the stored next id.
Looks up the original local def-id mapped to an AST node in `resolver.node_id_to_def_id` by calling `get` and `copied`.
Returns the possibly remapped local def-id for an AST node by calling `orig_opt_local_def_id` and then `get_remapped_def_id` on the result.
Returns the local def-id for an AST node, calling `opt_local_def_id` and panicking via `unwrap_or_else` if no mapping exists.

Resolves the innermost remapping for a local def-id from the `generics_def_id_map` stack by iterating in reverse and using `find_map`, `get`, and `copied`, falling back with `unwrap_or` to the original id when no remap exists.

Temporarily switches lowering state to a new HIR owner, runs the supplied lowering closure, packages the produced owner data, and restores the previous context. It calls `local_def_id` to resolve the owner, uses `std::mem::take`/`replace` to swap state, inserts the owner's zero local id with `insert`, invokes the closure `f(self)`, calls `make_owner_info` to build the final owner info, and finally records the owner in `children`.

Executes a closure with an additional generic def-id remapping layer active. It pushes the remap onto `generics_def_id_map`, calls the provided closure `f`, then pops the remap before returning the closure result.

Finalizes the accumulated data for one HIR owner into arena-allocated `OwnerInfo`. It takes the pending attrs, bodies, trait map, and inline-const flag, sorts bodies, builds a `SortedMap` with `from_presorted_elements`, calls `self.tcx.hash_owner_nodes(...)` to compute owner and attribute hashes, calls `index::index_hir` to build node and parenting indices, and allocates the resulting `hir::OwnerInfo` with `self.arena.alloc(...)`.

Maps an AST `NodeId` to a HIR id for the current owner, reusing an existing mapping or allocating a new local id. On a vacant entry it inserts the new local id, advances the counter with `increment_by`, calls `opt_local_def_id` to record nested def ownership in `children`, and transfers any pending trait candidates from `resolver.trait_map.remove(...)` into the local `trait_map`.
Allocates the next fresh `HirId` for the current owner by reading the current counter, incrementing it with `increment_by`, and returning the resulting owner/local-id pair.

Converts a resolver `Res<NodeId>` into a HIR `Res` by calling `apply_id` to rewrite each referenced node id through the current `node_id_to_local_id` mapping, using `get` and `copied` for lookup. If rewriting fails for an enclosing-owner local, it returns `Res::Err` via `unwrap_or`.
Obtains the full resolver result for a node id by calling `self.resolver.get_partial_res(id)` and converting it with `map_or(..., |pr| pr.expect_full_res())`, defaulting to `Res::Err` if missing.
Marks a span as desugared with the given reason and optional unstable allowances using the stable hashing context and current edition. It calls `with_stable_hashing_context` and `mark_with_reason`.
Adjusts a span for HIR lowering, attaching the current owner as the parent only when incremental compilation is enabled; otherwise returns the span unchanged.
Rebuilds an identifier with its span lowered for HIR. This method explicitly calls `lower_span`.

Converts a resolved lifetime into a HIR lifetime generic parameter, creating a new lifetime definition for fresh elided lifetimes and skipping `static`/error cases. It calls `create_def`, `lower_node_id`, `local_def_id`, and `lower_span`.

Lowers explicit binder generic parameters, appends resolver-provided extra lifetime parameters, and arena-allocates the combined HIR parameter list. It calls `lower_generic_params_mut`, `take_extra_lifetime_params`, and `lifetime_res_to_generic_param`.
Temporarily overrides the `is_in_dyn_type` flag while executing a closure, then restores the previous state.
Executes a closure in a fresh lowering scope by temporarily replacing current item, loop-condition, catch, and loop scope state, then restoring all previous values afterward.
Lowers and stores attributes for a HIR node, returning `None` for an empty attribute list. This method explicitly calls `lower_attr` for each attribute.
Lowers a single AST attribute by preserving its path/data structure, stripping tokens, lowering its arguments, and lowering its span. It calls `lower_attr_args` and `lower_span`.
Aliases already-lowered attributes from one HIR local id to another within the same owner when the target has stored attributes.

Lowers attribute arguments, recursively lowering delimited arguments and converting inert key-value literal expressions into HIR literal form, synthesizing an error literal when parsing fails. It calls `lower_delim_args` and `dcx`.
Lowers delimited attribute arguments by preserving delimiter/span data and flattening the token stream.

Lowers an associated type constraint, including its generic arguments, equality/const/type terms, and bound forms, while diagnosing invalid parenthesized or return-type-notation syntax. This method explicitly calls `lower_angle_bracketed_parameter_data`, `emit_bad_parenthesized_trait_in_assoc_ty`, `dcx`, `lower_ty`, `lower_anon_const`, `lower_param_bounds`, `lower_node_id`, and `lower_ident`.
Emits a diagnostic for illegal parenthesized associated type syntax, computing a targeted suggestion for either removing empty parentheses or replacing them with angle brackets. It calls `dcx`.

Lowers a generic argument as a lifetime, type, inferred arg, or const arg, including the path-type-to-const disambiguation path used for trivial const arguments. It calls `lower_lifetime`, `lower_node_id`, `lower_span`, `get_partial_res`, `next_node_id`, `create_def`, `with_new_scopes`, `lower_const_body`, `lower_ty`, and `lower_anon_const`.
Lowers an AST type and arena-allocates the resulting HIR type node. This method explicitly calls `lower_ty_direct`.

Lowers a path type, opportunistically converting a bare resolved trait path into a trait object when needed for fresh anonymous lifetimes; otherwise lowers it as a normal qpath type. It calls `get_partial_res`, `with_dyn_type_scope`, `lower_poly_trait_ref`, `elided_dyn_bound`, `lower_span`, `next_id`, `lower_node_id`, `lower_qpath`, and `ty_path`.
Constructs a HIR type node with a fresh `HirId` and lowered span. It calls `next_id` and `lower_span`.
Constructs a tuple HIR type from pre-lowered element types. This method explicitly calls `ty`.

Performs the main AST-to-HIR lowering for type syntax, handling anonymous ADTs, pointers/references, functions, tuples, paths, and other type forms while creating nested owners when required. This method explicitly calls `local_def_id`, `with_hir_id_owner`, `lower_field_def`, `lower_span`, `lower_ty`, `lower_mt`, `get_lifetime_res`, `next_node_id`, `lower_lifetime`, `lower_lifetime_binder`, `lower_safety`, `lower_extern`, `lower_fn_decl`, and `lower_fn_params_to_names`.

Lowers an `impl Trait` opaque type by marking its desugared span, determining which lifetimes must be captured or duplicated based on origin and precise captures, and delegating final opaque construction. It calls `mark_span_with_reason`, `take_extra_lifetime_params`, `lower_opaque_inner`, and `lower_param_bounds`.

Builds the internal HIR representation for an opaque type: creates the opaque definition, synthesizes duplicated lifetime parameters and mappings, lowers bounds under the remapping, lowers precise captures when present, and emits the owning `OpaqueTy` item plus returned `OpaqueDef` type. It calls `create_def`, `get_lifetime_res`, `dcx`, `next_node_id`, `lower_span`, `lower_ident`, `new_named_lifetime_with_res`, `local_def_id`, `with_hir_id_owner`, `with_remapping`, `lower_item_bounds`, `lower_precise_capturing_args`, and `lower_node_id`.

Extracts lowered parameter names from a function declaration, using the lowered identifier for simple identifier patterns and an empty placeholder ident otherwise. It calls `lower_ident` and `lower_span`.

Lowers a function signature by dropping the AST varargs sentinel, lowering each input type under the appropriate `impl Trait` policy, and lowering the return type either normally or through coroutine-specific opaque-return handling. It calls `lower_ty_direct`, `local_def_id`, `lower_coroutine_fn_ret_ty`, `lower_ty`, and `lower_span`.

Lowers a single generic bound into HIR, converting trait bounds and outlives bounds through the appropriate lowerers. It calls `lower_poly_trait_ref`, `lower_trait_bound_modifiers`, and `lower_lifetime`.
Lowers an AST lifetime by first calling `lower_ident` on the lifetime name, then calling `new_named_lifetime` with the original node id to build the HIR lifetime.

Constructs and arena-allocates a HIR lifetime from an explicit `LifetimeRes`, remapping parameter def-ids when needed via `get_remapped_def_id` or `local_def_id`, and filling the HIR node with `lower_node_id` and `lower_ident`.
Resolves a lifetime through `get_lifetime_res`, defaulting to `LifetimeRes::Error` on failure, then calls `new_named_lifetime_with_res` to produce the lowered HIR lifetime.
Returns an iterator that lowers each generic parameter by mapping the input slice and calling `lower_generic_param` for every element.
Lowers a slice of generic parameters into arena-allocated HIR output by calling `lower_generic_params_mut` and collecting the iterator with `alloc_from_iter`.

Lowers one generic parameter by calling `lower_generic_param_kind` to compute its HIR name and kind, then assigns ids/spans/attributes using `lower_node_id`, `lower_attrs`, `local_def_id`, and `lower_span`.

Lowers the kind-specific portion of a generic parameter. For lifetime params it queries `get_lifetime_res` and may call `lower_ident`; for type params it may emit diagnostics through `dcx` and lowers defaults with `lower_ty`; for const params it lowers the type with `lower_ty` and lowers any default const expression with `lower_anon_const`.
Lowers an AST trait reference by calling `lower_qpath`, requiring the result to be a resolved trait path, and then creating the HIR trait ref with `lower_node_id` for the reference id.
Lowers a poly trait reference by calling `lower_lifetime_binder` for bound generic params, `lower_trait_ref` for the trait itself, and `lower_span` for the resulting HIR span.
Lowers a mutable type by calling `lower_ty` on the inner type and preserving the mutability flag.
Lowers a slice of generic bounds into arena-allocated HIR bounds by calling `lower_param_bounds_mut` and collecting with `alloc_from_iter`.
Returns an iterator that lowers each generic bound by mapping the slice and calling `lower_param_bound` on each element.

Synthesizes a universal type parameter, its optional where-predicate, and the corresponding type path. It uses `local_def_id`, `lower_span`, `lower_node_id`, and `lower_ident` to build the parameter, calls `lower_generic_bound_predicate` to lower the bounds, and uses `next_id` plus arena allocation to construct the `TyKind::Path`.
Lowers an AST block expression by calling `lower_block` and then wrapping the result with `expr_block`.

Lowers an array length const expression. For `_`, it may create an inferred length using `lower_node_id` and `lower_span` when the feature is enabled; otherwise it reports instability and falls back to calling `lower_anon_const`. All non-underscore lengths are lowered by calling `lower_anon_const`.

Lowers an anonymous const inside fresh scopes by calling `with_new_scopes`; within that closure it uses `local_def_id`, `lower_node_id`, `lower_const_body`, and `lower_span`, then arena-allocates the resulting HIR anon const.
Maps the AST `UnsafeSource` enum directly to the corresponding HIR `UnsafeSource` variant without calling other methods from the list.
Builds a HIR statement by assigning a fresh id with `next_id` and lowering the statement span with `lower_span`.
Builds an expression statement by arena-allocating the expression and then calling `stmt` with `hir::StmtKind::Expr`.

Builds a `let` statement from a pre-lowered pattern and optional initializer. It assigns a fresh id with `next_id`, lowers the span with `lower_span`, stores statement attributes when present, and finally calls `stmt` after arena-allocating the `hir::LetStmt`.
Wraps a lowered expression in a block by calling `block_all` with no statements and the expression as the tail expression.
Constructs and arena-allocates a HIR block from statements and an optional tail expression, assigning a fresh block id with `next_id` and lowering the span with `lower_span`.
Builds a `ControlFlow::Continue` pattern by first calling `single_pat_field` for the payload and then calling `pat_lang_item_variant` with `hir::LangItem::ControlFlowContinue`.
Builds a `ControlFlow::Break` pattern by first calling `single_pat_field` for the payload and then calling `pat_lang_item_variant` with `hir::LangItem::ControlFlowBreak`.
Builds an `Option::Some` pattern by first calling `single_pat_field` for the contained pattern and then calling `pat_lang_item_variant` with `hir::LangItem::OptionSome`.
Builds an `Option::None` pattern by directly calling `pat_lang_item_variant` with `hir::LangItem::OptionNone` and no fields.
Creates a single tuple-struct-style pattern field for index 0, assigning a fresh field id with `next_id` and lowering the field spans with `lower_span`.
Builds a struct pattern referring to a lang item variant by lowering the span with `lower_span` to form a `QPath::LangItem`, then calling `pat` with `hir::PatKind::Struct`.
Builds an identifier pattern with the default binding mode by calling `pat_ident_binding_mode` with `hir::BindingMode::NONE`.

Convenience wrapper that creates a mutable identifier pattern using no explicit binding mode. It calls `pat_ident_binding_mode_mut` with `hir::BindingMode::NONE` and returns the resulting pattern and `HirId`.

Builds an identifier pattern with an explicit binding mode, then allocates it in the HIR arena. It calls `pat_ident_binding_mode_mut` to construct the `hir::Pat` and `self.arena.alloc` to return a shared HIR reference together with its `HirId`.

Constructs an owned `hir::Pat` for an identifier binding with the given binding mode. It calls `next_id` to assign a fresh `HirId`, `lower_ident` to lower the identifier, and `lower_span` to lower the source span.

Allocates a general HIR pattern with default binding modes enabled. It calls `next_id` to create the pattern’s `HirId`, `lower_span` to lower the span, and `self.arena.alloc` to store the pattern in the arena.
Constructs an owned HIR pattern like `pat`, but with `default_binding_modes` disabled. It calls `next_id` for a fresh `HirId` and `lower_span` for the lowered span.

Builds a `hir::Ty` from a qualified path, rewriting resolved trait or trait-alias paths into `hir::TyKind::TraitObject`. In that trait-object case it calls `lower_span` to build the `PolyTraitRef`, `next_id` to give the outer `Ty` a new id, and `elided_dyn_bound` to supply the implicit `dyn` lifetime bound; it also calls `lower_span` again for the final type span.

Creates and arena-allocates an implicit object lifetime bound used for elided `dyn` lifetimes. It calls `next_id` to assign a `HirId`, `lower_span` to lower the span used in the lifetime identifier, and `self.arena.alloc` to return the allocated lifetime.

If the `effects` feature is enabled, lowers a bound constness marker into a synthetic const generic argument and appends it to the argument list. For `Always` and `Maybe` it calls `lcx.lower_span` to lower spans; in the `Maybe` case it may call `lcx.dcx().span_delayed_bug` when `host_param_id` is missing, otherwise it calls `lcx.next_id` to build the host path. After selecting the expression body, it calls `lcx.lower_body` and inside that closure `lcx.expr` to lower the const expression, then calls `lcx.next_node_id`, `lcx.next_id`, and `lcx.create_def` to create the anonymous const, and finally pushes the resulting const argument into `self.args`.
Checks whether the generic-argument builder contains no args, no bindings, and no parenthesized form. It does not call any other methods from the provided list.

Finalizes the builder into an arena-allocated `hir::GenericArgs`. It calls `this.arena.alloc_from_iter` to allocate the argument list, `this.lower_span` to lower the stored span, and `this.arena.alloc` to allocate the completed `hir::GenericArgs`.
Trait requirement for retrieving legacy const-generic argument rewrite indices for an expression; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Trait requirement for fetching the partial name-resolution result for a node; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Trait requirement for fetching per-namespace import resolutions for a node; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Trait requirement for looking up the resolved target of a label; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Trait requirement for retrieving the resolved lifetime for a node; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Trait requirement for removing and returning extra synthesized lifetime parameters associated with a node; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Trait requirement for moving stored extra lifetime parameters from one node ID to another; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Trait requirement for querying the declaration macro kind of a local definition; this declaration has no body and does not call other methods in the Methods List.

Returns legacy const-generic rewrite positions only for path expressions that name a non-local function, have no explicit generic arguments, and have resolver-provided rewrite data; otherwise returns None. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Looks up and copies the stored partial resolution for the given node ID from the resolver map. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Returns the stored per-namespace import resolution for the given node ID, defaulting to an empty result when absent. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Looks up and copies the resolved label target node ID for the given node. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Looks up and copies the resolved lifetime information for the given node ID. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Removes and returns any extra lifetime parameters recorded for the given node ID, or an empty list if none exist. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Moves extra lifetime parameters from one node ID entry to another by removing the source entry and inserting it under the destination ID. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Returns the recorded builtin macro kind for a local definition, defaulting to bang macros when no entry is present. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.

Checks whether `impl Trait` is permitted in parameter position for this function-declaration kind, allowing only free functions, inherent methods, impl methods, and trait methods. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.

Checks whether `impl Trait` is permitted in return position for this function-declaration kind, returning true for free functions, inherent methods, impl methods, and trait methods. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Extracts the fully resolved imported items for a `use` item from the resolver. It calls `impl ResolverAstLoweringExt for ResolverAstLowering::get_import_res`.
Returns the session diagnostic handler used by lowering for error reporting. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.

Lowers an `async fn` return type into the desugared opaque `impl Future` HIR return, collecting captured extra lifetimes, building the async opaque type, and wrapping it as `FnRetTy::Return`. It calls `impl ResolverAstLoweringExt for ResolverAstLowering::take_extra_lifetime_params` and `impl<'a, 'hir> LoweringContext<'a, 'hir>::lower_async_fn_output_type_to_future_bound`.

Builds the `Future<Output = T>` bound used in async-fn desugaring by lowering the explicit return type or synthesizing `()` for default returns, then packaging it as a `Future` lang-item trait bound. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.

Converts an AST trait-bound modifier into its HIR form, gating negative bounds on the corresponding feature flag and choosing placeholder HIR variants for invalid parsed combinations so lowering can continue. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.

Converts a HIR lifetime into a semantic `ty::Region` by resolving named bound variables, early-bound parameters, free regions, and error cases, and falls back to inference or an error region for unresolved elided lifetimes. This method explicitly calls `tcx` and `re_infer`.

Builds instantiated generic arguments for a type path segment and rejects associated type bindings in plain type position before returning the resulting `GenericArgsRef`. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_path` and `tcx`.

Core generic-argument instantiation routine for a path: it validates generic arity, handles parent and `Self` arguments, and constructs substitutions by combining explicit HIR arguments with defaults or inference through the local `SubstsForAstPathCtxt` helper. This method explicitly calls `tcx`.

Returns the stored HIR generic arguments only when the queried `DefId` matches the current target definition; otherwise reports that no explicit args are available. It does not call other methods in this file.

Converts an explicit lifetime, type, inferred type, const, or inferred const HIR argument into a `ty::GenericArg`, including optional stability checks and special handling for `_` in type positions. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `allow_ty_infer`, `ast_ty_to_ty`, `ast_region_to_region`, and `ct_infer`.

Synthesizes a missing generic argument by inferring lifetimes, inferring types, applying type defaults, or inferring/defaulting consts while guarding against prior type errors. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `re_infer`, `ty_infer`, and `ct_infer`.

Separately converts associated type/const bindings and constraint clauses from HIR generic arguments into `ConvertedBinding` records for later predicate generation. This method explicitly calls `ast_ty_to_ty` and `tcx`.

Builds instantiated generic arguments for an associated item path using inherited parent arguments, then rejects associated type bindings in this plain associated-item argument position. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_path` and `tcx`.

Creates a monomorphic trait reference from a parsed trait path and explicit `Self` type after first forbidding generics on all non-final path segments. This method explicitly calls `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_mono_trait_ref`.

Internal worker for poly trait-ref instantiation: it builds trait generic arguments, collects associated bindings, creates a bound `TraitRef`, pushes the trait bound into `Bounds`, and converts associated bindings into predicates while handling invalid negative-bound bindings. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_path`, `tcx`, `create_assoc_bindings_for_generic_args`, and `add_predicates_for_ast_type_binding`.

Top-level entry point for instantiating a parsed trait bound into polymorphic bounds data: it extracts the final path segment, rejects generics on earlier segments, checks for internal `Fn`-trait diagnostics, and delegates the actual construction to `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`. This method explicitly calls `prohibit_generics`, `complain_about_internal_fn_trait`, and `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`.

Instantiates a trait bound for a lang-item trait by resolving the lang item to a trait `DefId`, fabricating an invalid path segment placeholder, and delegating to `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`. This method explicitly calls `tcx` and `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`.

Builds a non-polymorphic `ty::TraitRef` from a trait path segment and `Self` type by first creating trait arguments and then rejecting associated type bindings in this context. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_trait_ref` and `tcx`.

Constructs generic arguments for a trait reference path, after first issuing diagnostics for internal `Fn`-trait usage, by delegating to the general path-argument builder with the supplied `Self` type. This method explicitly calls `complain_about_internal_fn_trait` and `create_args_for_ast_path`.
Checks whether a trait defines an associated item of the given kind and name by querying `tcx().associated_items(...)`, calling `find_by_name_and_kind`, and returning whether the result `is_some()`.

Converts a resolved type path into a `Ty` by first calling `ast_path_args_for_ty` to build generic arguments, then either constructing a lazy type-alias `Ty::new_alias` when `def_kind`/`type_alias_is_lazy` indicate a lazy alias, or instantiating `tcx.at(span).type_of(did)` with those args.

Builds and emits the E0223 ambiguous-associated-type diagnostic, checking `tcx().resolutions(())` for the std-module confusion case and otherwise assembling context-sensitive suggestions with `span_suggestion_verbose` or `span_suggestions` before `emit()`.

Finds the unique trait bound on a type parameter that defines a named associated item by calling `get_type_parameter_bounds` to collect predicates and then delegating to `one_bound_for_assoc_type`, supplying candidates produced from `traits::transitive_bounds_that_define_assoc_item`.

Selects a single trait bound that defines the requested associated type or const by filtering candidates with `trait_defines_associated_item_named`; if none match it calls `complain_about_assoc_type_not_found`, and if multiple incompatible matches remain it emits ambiguity diagnostics using `tcx().associated_items(...).find_by_name_and_kind` and trait-path formatting before returning the chosen bound.

Selects a single trait bound that defines the requested associated method by filtering candidates with `trait_defines_associated_item_named`; if no match or multiple matches exist, it emits the corresponding error via `tcx().sess.emit_err`, otherwise it returns the unique candidate.

Resolves a type-relative path like `T::Assoc` by first probing ADTs with `probe_adt` to detect enum variants or inherent associated types, using `prohibit_generics` for invalid variant generics, then calling `lookup_inherent_assoc_ty` for inherent associated types or `one_bound_for_assoc_type` over trait/supertrait candidates to produce the final associated type, while also performing stability and diagnostic handling through `tcx` queries.

Searches inherent impls of an ADT for an applicable inherent associated type: it gathers raw candidates by calling `lookup_assoc_ty_unchecked`, then uses an inference context and normalization/obligation checking to filter applicable impls, and finally instantiates the selected associated type with `fresh_args_for_item`, `type_of`, and `instantiate`.
Returns the folder’s `TyCtxt` interner.
Erases late-bound regions during folding by checking `is_late_bound` and replacing such regions with `re_erased`, leaving other regions unchanged.
Replaces bound types with placeholders by matching on `kind()` for `ty::Bound` and otherwise recursively folding substructure via `super_fold_with`.
Replaces bound consts with placeholder consts after asserting `ty().has_escaping_bound_vars()` is false; for non-bound consts it recurses with `super_fold_with`.
Looks up an associated type in a scope by calling `lookup_assoc_ty_unchecked`, validating the result with `check_assoc_ty`, and returning the associated item `DefId` if found.

Performs unchecked associated-type lookup in a scope by adjusting the identifier with `tcx.adjust_ident_and_get_scope`, scanning `tcx.associated_items(scope).in_definition_order()`, and returning the matching type-namespace item together with the resolved scope.
Verifies that an associated type is accessible and stable by checking `tcx.visibility(item).is_accessible_from(...)`, emitting a privacy error if needed, and then calling `tcx.check_stability`.

Finds accessible traits whose associated types could match a given `qself_ty` by scanning `tcx.all_traits()`, filtering traits with a matching associated type in `associated_items`, checking visibility, and testing impl self-types for unification with an inference context before collecting trait path strings.

Converts a qualified path `<Self as Trait>::Assoc` into a projection type; when `Self` is omitted it gathers candidate implementing type names and calls `report_ambiguous_associated_type` to emit an error, otherwise it builds the trait ref with `ast_path_to_mono_trait_ref`, creates item args with `create_args_for_associated_item`, and returns `Ty::new_projection`.

Rejects generic arguments and associated type bindings on path segments that must not have them: it scans the segments’ args to classify forbidden lifetime/type/const/infer arguments, emits a tailored diagnostic through the supplied `extend` callback, and calls `prohibit_assoc_ty_binding` for associated type bindings.

Reconstructs which path segments in a value path carry generic arguments by analyzing the resolved `DefKind`, querying `tcx.generics_of`, and in ADT-related cases using `probe_adt`/parent relationships to produce a sequence of `PathSeg` entries describing the relevant definition and segment index.

Converts a resolved HIR path into a type by dispatching on `path.res`: it calls `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_args_for_ty` for opaque types, `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_ty` for ordinary nominal types, `def_ids_for_value_path_segments` plus `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_ty` for variant paths, `associated_path_to_ty` for type-relative paths, and `hir_id_to_bound_ty` for type parameters, while also emitting diagnostics for invalid resolutions.

Converts a HIR id for a bound type parameter into a `Ty` by querying `tcx.named_bound_var`: late-bound parameters become `Ty::new_bound`, early-bound parameters use `hir().ty_param_owner` plus `generics_of` to build `Ty::new_param`, and error resolutions become `Ty::new_error`.

Converts a HIR id for a bound const parameter into a `Const` by querying `tcx.named_bound_var`: early-bound parameters use `parent` and `generics_of` to build `Const::new_param`, late-bound parameters become `Const::new_bound`, and error resolutions become `Const::new_error`.
Converts a HIR type into a semantic type by calling `ast_ty_to_ty_inner` with the default non-borrowed, non-path flags.
Converts a HIR type appearing inside a path by calling `ast_ty_to_ty_inner` with `in_path` enabled.

Core recursive HIR-type conversion routine. It converts slices, pointers, refs, tuples, bare fns, trait objects, paths, opaque defs, and type-relative paths by calling other helpers such as `ast_ty_to_ty`, `ast_region_to_region`, `ty_of_fn`, `maybe_lint_bare_trait`, `conv_object_ty_poly_trait_ref`, `res_to_ty`, `impl_trait_ty_to_ty`, and `associated_path_to_ty`, then constructs the corresponding `Ty` node.

Builds the type for an `impl Trait`/opaque definition by iterating the item generics, resolving explicit lifetime arguments with `ast_region_to_region`, filling other parameters from `mk_param_from_def`, and then returning either `Ty::new_projection` for trait context or `Ty::new_opaque` otherwise.
Computes an argument type, reusing an expected type for `_` arguments by calling `record_ty`, and otherwise delegating to `ast_ty_to_ty`.

Constructs a function signature from HIR by collecting late-bound vars, walking generics for placeholder detection, converting inputs with `ty_of_arg`, converting the return type with `ast_ty_to_ty` when present, building the signature with `mk_fn_sig`/`bind_with_vars`, optionally calling `suggest_trait_fn_ty_for_impl_fn_infer` for `_` recovery, and finally validating region usage with `validate_late_bound_regions` after computing constrained and referenced late-bound regions.

When an impl method uses `_` in its signature, tries to recover the corresponding trait method type by computing the impl’s trait ref with `instantiate_mono_trait_ref` and `ast_ty_to_ty`, locating the associated method via `associated_items(...).find_by_name_and_kind`, instantiating its `fn_sig`, liberating late-bound regions, and returning the requested input or output type.

Checks that every referenced late-bound region is constrained by iterating `referenced_regions.difference(&constrained_regions)`, creating each diagnostic with `generate_err`, adding explanatory notes for anonymous lifetimes, and emitting the error.

Computes the lifetime bound for a trait object from its existential predicates when no explicit bound is given. It calls `tcx` to access the type context and `object_region_bounds` to derive candidate region bounds; if the derived set `is_empty`, it returns `None` so the caller can use the default. It then uses `iter`/`any` together with `is_static` to prefer `'static` when present, and otherwise checks whether all derived bounds are the same; if multiple distinct bounds exist, it calls `emit_err` to report an ambiguous lifetime bound before returning one of the derived regions.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/wf: Returns the underlying `ObligationCtxt` by dereferencing `WfCheckingCtxt`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context inside the obligation context; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Normalizes a type-foldable value under the current parameter environment, attaching a `WellFormed` obligation cause for diagnostics; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Builds and registers a `WellFormed` predicate obligation for a generic argument using the current body and parameter environment. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`.

Creates the temporary inference/obligation context used for well-formedness checking, runs the supplied checker closure, solves obligations, computes implied bounds, lints redundant lifetimes, and resolves/report regions with a compatibility path for some implied-bounds cases; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Top-level dispatcher that selects the appropriate WF checker for the HIR node kind and then checks each generic parameter. It calls `check_item`, `check_trait_item`, `check_impl_item`, `check_foreign_item`, `check_item_type`, and `check_param_wf`.

Checks item-level well-formedness after precollecting item types, handling impls, functions, statics/consts/type aliases, ADTs, and traits according to item kind. It calls `check_impl`, `check_item_fn`, `check_item_type`, `check_type_defn`, and `check_trait`.
Checks a foreign item after precollecting its type information, validating foreign functions and statics while accepting foreign types unchanged. It calls `check_item_fn` and `check_item_type`.

Checks a trait item by precollecting its types, diagnosing misuse of the trait name as an unboxed self trait object, validating the associated item itself, and also validating synthesized associated types for RPITIT methods. It calls `check_dyn_incompatible_self_trait_by_name` and `check_associated_item`.

Analyzes generic associated types across all associated items of a trait to infer potentially missing outlives bounds by repeatedly intersecting constraints discovered from method signatures and other bounds. It calls `gather_gat_bounds`, `augment_param_env`, `region_known_to_outlive`, and `ty_known_to_outlive`.

Extends a parameter environment with additional clause predicates, returning the original environment unchanged when no new predicates are provided; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Collects GAT arguments appearing in a type/signature and derives required outlives clauses by checking whether referenced types or regions are known to outlive each region argument. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit`, `ty_known_to_outlive`, and `region_known_to_outlive`.
Tests whether a type is known to outlive a region under the current environment by creating a region obligation probe. It calls `test_region_obligations`.
Tests whether one region is known to outlive another under the current environment by probing a subregion constraint. It calls `test_region_obligations`.

Builds a fresh inference context, computes implied outlives bounds for the provided well-formed types, lets the caller add extra region constraints, resolves regions, and returns whether no region errors occurred. It calls `infer_ctxt`, `build`, `implied_bounds_tys`, `with_bounds`, `region_bound_pairs`, the passed-in `add_constraints`, `resolve_regions`, and `is_empty`.

Creates a default `GATSubstCollector` for the target GAT, visits the given foldable value to collect referenced region and type substitutions, and returns the collected sets. It calls `default` and `visit_with`.

Visits a type, and when it finds a projection alias for the tracked GAT, scans its generic arguments to record non-bound lifetime substitutions and type substitutions along with their argument indices, then continues recursive traversal. It calls `kind`, `iter`, `enumerate`, `unpack`, `is_bound`, `insert`, and `super_visit_with`.

Returns whether a HIR type syntactically looks like a single-segment trait object naming the enclosing trait, indicating it may have meant `Self`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Checks whether a trait item mistakenly refers to its own trait name where `Self` is intended, and emits a suggestion-based diagnostic when this makes the trait non-object-safe. It calls `could_be_self` to detect suspicious type references in associated const/type/function signatures and calls `is_object_safe` to skip diagnostics for object-safe traits.

Checks an impl item after precollecting its types, choosing an appropriate diagnostic span for methods and associated types before delegating to associated-item WF checking. It calls `check_associated_item`.

Checks generic-parameter well-formedness, focusing on const parameters: it either enforces the relevant lang-item trait bound in a WF context on feature-enabled paths or emits structural-match style diagnostics on stable paths. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt` and contains the local helper `ty_is_local`.
Local helper used by `check_param_wf` to decide whether a const-parameter type is local by recursively inspecting ADTs, arrays, slices, shared references, and tuples. It calls itself recursively.

Runs WF checking for an associated const, function, or type inside a dedicated context, ensuring trait coherence first, computing the appropriate `Self` type, and then validating the item-specific signature or value/type. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_associated_type_bounds`.

Maps an `ItemKind` to its corresponding `AdtKind`, returning `Some(Struct)`, `Some(Union)`, or `Some(Enum)` for ADT items and `None` for all other item kinds. It does not call any other methods from the provided Methods List.

Checks structs, unions, and enums for representability and field/type well-formedness, enforces `Sized` where required for non-tail fields or packed/drop-sensitive layouts, registers extra obligations such as const evaluatability, and validates where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks a trait item by rejecting associated items on marker traits, validating the trait's where-clauses in a WF context, and then running the GAT missing-bound analysis for real traits. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `check_where_clauses`, and `check_gat_where_clauses`.

Validates explicit bounds on a trait associated type by normalizing each bound, expanding it into clause well-formedness obligations, and registering those obligations. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx` and `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`.
Checks a free or foreign function signature inside a dedicated WF context using the instantiated function signature. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`.

Checks the declared type of an item in a WF context by normalizing it, registering its well-formedness, optionally enforcing `Sized` depending on unsized-handling rules, and requiring `Sync` for eligible shared statics. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.

Checks an impl in a WF context by validating either the implemented trait reference and its derived obligations or the inherent self type, then validating the impl's where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks where-clauses and generic defaults for well-formedness by registering obligations for concrete default types/consts, examining predicate dependencies, normalizing predicates, and feeding the resulting obligations into the current WF context. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.
Visits a type, records the index of any `ty::Param` encountered in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.
Stops traversal when a region is encountered by immediately returning `ControlFlow::Break(())`; it does not call other methods from the list.
Visits a const, records the index of any const generic parameter found in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.

Well-formedness-checks a function or method signature by liberating late-bound regions, normalizing each input/output type with per-parameter locations, registering WF obligations for every input/output type, and checking where-clauses. It explicitly calls `check_where_clauses` and uses `register_bound` to enforce the tuple and `Sized` requirements for `Abi::RustCall` arguments.

Validates a method's `self` receiver by normalizing the method signature, `self_ty`, and receiver type, then checking receiver legality. It explicitly calls `receiver_is_valid`, potentially multiple times under different feature configurations, to decide whether the receiver is accepted or which diagnostic to emit.

Emits error E0307 for an invalid `self` parameter type, adding an explanatory note and help text before returning the emitted diagnostic. It directly calls `dcx`, `with_note`, `with_help`, and `emit`.

Determines whether a method receiver type is valid for a given `Self` type by first trying direct type equality, then autodereferencing toward `self_ty`, registering autoderef obligations on success. When arbitrary self types are not enabled, it explicitly calls `receiver_is_implemented` at each deref step and also registers the corresponding `Receiver` bound before continuing.

Checks whether a candidate receiver type satisfies the `Receiver` lang-item trait by building the trait obligation and testing it with `predicate_must_hold_modulo_regions`; it does not call other methods from the list.

Checks that generic parameters of an ADT or lazy type alias are sufficiently constrained for variance computation, skipping items whose field/alias types already contain errors. It explicitly calls `identify_constrained_generic_params` to extend the constrained set and `report_bivariance` to emit diagnostics for unconstrained parameters.

Builds and emits the diagnostic for an unused/bivariant generic parameter, selecting item-specific help text and collecting spans where the parameter or `Self` alias appears. It explicitly calls `IsProbablyCyclical::visit_def` to detect likely recursive ADTs/type aliases so it can report recursive-usage diagnostics instead of plain unused-parameter errors.

Finds elaborated predicates on the current item that are globally true but nontrivial, normalizes them, refines their source span to the matching predicate clause when possible, and registers them as `TrivialBound` obligations. It does not call other methods from the provided list.

Runs well-formedness checking over all items, impl items, trait items, foreign items, and opaques in a module in parallel, combining their results, and checks for the crate entry function at the crate root. It explicitly calls `check_well_formed` for each covered definition.
Constructs and returns the E0392 diagnostic for an unused parameter and adds a span label marking it as unused. It calls `dcx` and `with_span_label`.
Registers this module's query providers by installing `check_mod_type_wf` and `check_well_formed` into the compiler provider table. It explicitly references `check_mod_type_wf` from the methods list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_infer/src/infer/opaque_ty: Scans a foldable value for local opaque aliases that are currently definable in this context, replaces each eligible opaque with a fresh inference type variable, and accumulates the resulting obligations. It first short-circuits when `next_trait_solver` is enabled or `has_opaque_types` is false, and for each matched opaque it calls `opaque_type_origin` to decide eligibility and `handle_opaque_type` to relate the new inference variable back to the opaque definition.

Handles the relation between an opaque type and another type during inference, ignoring error types, orienting the comparison by `a_is_expected`, and only treating local opaque aliases as definitional when they are valid for the current `DefiningAnchor`. When the opaque is allowed to be defined here, it calls `opaque_type_origin` to validate the defining context and then calls `register_hidden_type` to record the inferred hidden type; otherwise it emits diagnostics for invalid defining-use situations such as problematic opaque-to-opaque cases.

Resolves the concrete hidden type, computes the invariant lifetime arguments of the opaque plus `'static` as the allowed choice set, and visits the hidden type to constrain every free region to one of those choices. It calls `member_constraint` through the region visitor callback for each discovered region.

Determines whether a local opaque type is being defined from the current defining-use anchor and, if so, returns its `OpaqueTyOrigin`. For type-alias opaques it checks associated-type definitions via `opaque_types_defined_by` and otherwise calls `may_define_opaque_type` to decide whether the current item may define the opaque.
Visits inside binders without stopping, delegating traversal to `super_visit_with` and then continuing.
Processes each encountered region for opaque-member checking, skipping bound regions and invoking the stored callback for all other regions.

Traverses only types that contain free regions and selectively visits the parts relevant for opaque lifetime constraints. It skips enclosing-item lifetimes for closures and coroutines by manually visiting captured/upvar and signature-related components, visits only non-bivariant arguments of nested opaque aliases, and otherwise falls back to `super_visit_with`.
Returns whether this `UseKind` represents a defining use, yielding true for `DefiningUse` and false for `OpaqueUse`.

Registers an inferred hidden type for an opaque definition and produces the obligations needed to justify it. It calls `insert_hidden_type` to store or unify the hidden type in the opaque-type table, then calls `add_item_bounds_for_hidden_type` to add the opaque item's declared bounds as obligations on that hidden type.

Inserts a hidden type candidate into inference state for an opaque key. In intercrate mode it adds an ambiguous obligation instead of defining the opaque; otherwise it registers the hidden type in the opaque storage, and if a previous hidden type was already present it calls `eq_exp` to equate the old and new hidden types and extends the obligation list with the resulting obligations.

Instantiates the explicit bounds declared on an opaque item, rewrites them so they apply to the inferred hidden type, and pushes each rewritten predicate as an obligation. While folding each predicate, it calls `infer_projection` to replace eligible projection aliases with inference variables, and it substitutes self-references to the same opaque alias with `hidden_ty` before creating obligations.
Checks whether a named opaque type may be defined from the given local item by walking up the HIR parent chain from the item to see whether it reaches the opaque type’s defining scope.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_borrowck/src/type_check/r: Entry point for relating two MIR types under a given variance and constraint category. It constructs an `NllTypeRelating` engine with `NllTypeRelating::new`, computes diagnostics context with `UniverseInfo::relate`, and then calls `relate` to perform the actual comparison and constraint generation.

Relates two generic-argument lists for invariant equality. It constructs an `NllTypeRelating` engine with `NllTypeRelating::new`, uses `UniverseInfo::other` and invariant variance, and then calls `relate` on the argument lists.

Constructs an `NllTypeRelatingDelegate` by storing the provided type-checking context, locations, constraint category, and universe diagnostic info. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns the source span for the current MIR location by querying `self.locations.span(self.type_checker.body)`. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns the `ParamEnv` stored in the enclosing `TypeChecker`. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Creates a fresh inference universe via the inference context, records the associated `UniverseInfo` in the borrow-checker constraint store, and returns the new universe index. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Allocates and returns a fresh existential NLL region variable, tagging its origin as existential and preserving whether it came from a `forall`. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
